final_answer:
In a system where prices are determined by the interaction of buyers and sellers, the price of a good or service is influenced by two key factors: the quantity of the item available (supply) and the number of people wanting to purchase it (demand). When many people want to buy something but not enough is available, the price tends to rise. Conversely, if there is an abundance of the item and few people want it, the price tends to fall. This natural balance between what is available and what is desired helps set the price.

When a rule is introduced that limits how high a price can go, it can disrupt this balance. If the set price is lower than what would naturally occur, it may result in a situation where there isn't enough of the item available to meet the demand. This can lead to long waits, reduced quality, or alternative methods of obtaining the item outside of the usual channels.
